Brief.md
# Brief — idea of the study

## Question
With network interference, how accurate is the regression-based GATE estimator (fit outcome on functions of the assignment vector — own treatment, treated-neighbour fraction/count, higher-order terms — then predict at all-treated and all-control and difference; Chin 2019, Han & Ugander 2023)? What determines its error, and under which interference mechanisms, networks and designs does it hold or fail?

## Thesis (the claim the paper is built around)
The regression GATE estimator is not mainly limited by sample size. It is limited by **extrapolation to the global-treatment corner**. Under a Bernoulli(p) experiment the exposure features of almost every unit sit near p; the GATE needs the model at exposure 1 and 0. Define the extrapolation distance
D = Mahalanobis distance of the mean counterfactual feature vector (all-treated, all-control) from the observed feature distribution, computed from the assignment and the graph only. For a treated-neighbour-fraction feature on a degree-d unit, D^2 ≈ d(1-p)/p (all-treated) and d·p/(1-p) (all-control): it grows with degree and is balanced only at p = 1/2.
Predictions, each falsifiable:
- P1 (variance, correct linear specification): RMSE ∝ sqrt(D^2/n)-type scaling; denser networks make the regression estimator *worse* at fixed n despite equal interference strength; the DM bias does not grow with d the same way.
- P2 (bias, curved response — saturation, threshold/complex contagion, two-hop diffusion): bias ≈ curvature × extrapolation distance, not removable by a more flexible learner (trees extrapolate flat; polynomials explode). Flexible regressors do not beat linear regression on GATE error although they win on in-sample prediction.
- P3 (design): graph-cluster randomization shrinks D (exposures concentrate near 0/1), so regression + cluster design beats either alone in a band of cluster-able graphs, and loses that benefit when modularity is low (e.g. Stanford3-type dense graphs) because cluster-level effective sample size drops.
- P4 (treatment probability): the error is minimised near p = 1/2 for symmetric corners; small p amplifies the all-treated extrapolation.
- P5 (diagnostic): D, and the disagreement between feature specifications at the counterfactual points, predict the realised error across settings (rank correlation on held-out settings) and flag failure better than the estimator's own bootstrap CI, whose coverage collapses exactly where D is large. If P5 fails, that is reported as the finding and its reason analysed.
- Regression beats DM only below a data-computable D / interference-strength threshold; above it a regression estimate can be worse than the biased DM. The paper maps this regime and states its boundary.

## Contribution over prior work
Chin 2019 and Han–Ugander 2023 propose the estimators and show they can work; the design-based literature (Aronow–Samii, Ugander et al., Eckles et al., Leung, Li–Wager) analyses HT/Hájek with correctly specified exposures. What is open, and what this study provides, is an *explanation and a map of regression-GATE error*: its decomposition into extrapolation bias and counterfactual-leverage variance, a diagnostic computable from one experiment, the interaction with the design (cluster randomization) and with network family/degree/p, honest regimes where regression fails or is dominated, and a test of whether flexible/graph learners help. No new estimator is the claim; a verified, predictive account of when to trust the existing one is. Positive or negative outcomes of P1–P5 are all reported; a failed P5 (D does not predict error) would itself be a main negative result.

## Study design (what the idea asks of the analysis)
- **Estimand**: GATE τ = mean_i[Y_i(1)] − mean_i[Y_i(0)], exact in simulation (noise-free outcome function evaluated at 1 and 0).
- **Networks**: synthetic ER/SBM/BA/Watts–Strogatz with n ∈ 10^3–10^4 and mean degree swept ~5–100; real: socfb-Stanford3 (1

# idea-repo

ResearchWorld role: idea-repo# Prior work and how the study relates to it

Keys refer to `prior_work.bib`. Only entries checked on 2026-11-25 are listed. The papers' details beyond the abstracts have not all been read; the report role should read a source before attributing a specific theorem to it.

## Closest work (the study must be positioned against these)

- **Chin 2019** (`chin2019regression`): the regression-adjustment GATE estimator itself (fit a model of outcome on functions of the assignment vector, predict at all-treated / all-control, difference), with linear-model properties and resampling inference. The study uses it as the primary object. Open: no systematic account of when its error is large, no comparison across interference forms, network families and designs, no data-computable warning.
- **Han & Ugander 2023** (`han2023model`): model-based regression adjustment with generated graph/treatment covariates, block-bootstrap CIs, semi-synthetic and real checks. Baseline (richer covariate set) and the closest competitor for "which features". Open: the error is not explained by a quantity that can be computed before/after the experiment.
- **Gao & Ding 2023** (`gao2023causal`): regression-based analysis of network experiments with design-based properties. Closest design-based treatment of regression estimators; to be read in detail before the paper states what is new.
- **Aronow & Samii 2017, Ugander et al. 2013, Eckles et al. 2017** (`aronow2017estimating`, `ugander2013graph`, `eckles2017design`): exposure-mapping HT/Hájek estimators, graph cluster randomization, neighbourhood-fraction exposures. Baselines (HT/Hájek with fraction-threshold exposure; DM under cluster randomization) and the source of the designs we cross with the regression estimator.
- **Cortez et al. 2022** (`cortez2022staggered`): staggered rollout, polynomial (low-order interaction) estimator without network knowledge. Different design; an optional baseline where the network is unknown.

## Related methods and theory

- Unknown / approximate interference: `savje2021average` (DM is consistent for a marginalised estimand — shows what DM estimates), `leung2022causal`, `savje2023causal` (misspecified exposure mappings: separate estimand and assumption — our setting is exactly estimand = GATE with a possibly misspecified model), `yu2022estimating` (unknown network).
- Designs: `leung2022rate`, `ugander2023randomized`, `candogan2023correlated`, `basse2018designs`, `karrer2021network`, `gui2015network`, `chen2023optimized` (HT estimator and covariance design under one-hop model).
- Theory under random graphs / linear interference: `li2022random`, `sussman2017elements`, `hu2022average`.
- Graph learners as optional regressors: `kipf2017semi`, `defferrard2016convolutional`.

## What the study takes from them and adds

Takes: the GATE estimand, Bernoulli and graph-cluster designs, exposure-mapping HT/Hájek and DM as baselines, Chin's estimator and Han–Ugander's covariates as the regression family.
Adds (the claimed contribution, see the Brief): a diagnosis of regression-GATE error as extrapolation to the global-treatment corner, a quantity computable from the experiment that predicts the error, a regime map over interference form × network family × design × treatment probability × degree, and a falsifiable test of the scaling predictions, with negative results reported.

## Data
`traud2012social`, `rossi2015network` (socfb-Stanford3, CC BY-SA), `mcauley2012learning` (ego-Facebook).

## Access restriction
The objective bars one published paper that studied this question. No search made so far targeted it; searches were by generic topic and by known titles listed here. Nothing encountered looked like it. If a later search surfaces such a page, stop reading and record it in the reproduction notes.

mkdir -p /hutian/tmp && cd /hutian/tmp && cat > review1.md <<'EOF'
# Review of the idea (Brief, 2026-11-25 19:00 revision) — round 1

Reviewer: `idea-review-repo`. Scope: the Brief and `prior_work.md`/`.bib` as pushed (b35d76a). The outline does not exist yet, so the plan is not reviewed here. Nothing below asks you to narrow the study; the first four items are what would make the central claim *correct*, the rest make it testable and affordable.

## What is strong (keep it)
- A single thesis (error is limited by extrapolation to the global-treatment corner, not by n) with falsifiable P1–P5, and an explicit commitment to report P5 failing as a result.
- Exact estimand in simulation, mechanism list frozen before results, additions labelled exploratory, strength calibrated through the DM bias.
- Right comparison set (DM, HT/Hájek, cluster designs, Chin, Han–Ugander, oracle spec), real graphs used for what the claim is about, and a metric list with reasons (sign-error rate, coverage, bias/variance split).
- The "what would change the idea" paragraph: claim widens, not narrows.

## Major issues

**1. One quantity D is asked to explain two different errors; they scale differently.**
For the regression GATE τ̂ = Δxᵀβ̂ (Δx = mean counterfactual feature difference), the *variance* is governed by the Mahalanobis form ΔxᵀΣ⁻¹Δx/n, as the Brief says. The *bias* from a curved response is not: for a response g(f) in treated-neighbour fraction, the linear fit is tangent near p and the bias is ≈ ½ g''·(1−p)², a function of the **raw** distance in exposure units, which does *not* grow with degree d (the Mahalanobis D² ≈ d(1−p)/p does). For count-type/threshold mechanisms the dependence on d is different again. So P2 as written ("bias ≈ curvature × extrapolation distance" with D defined in Mahalanobis units) will probably fail on the d-dependence for the fraction feature, for a reason known in advance. Please (a) state separate predicted scalings for bias (raw distance × curvature, per mechanism) and variance (D²/n), (b) make P5's diagnostic two-part (leverage D, plus a curvature/specification-disagreement term) and say what each is expected to predict. Otherwise "D fails" will be reported for a reason that is a formulation error, not a finding.

**2. P1 is close to a textbook identity; say where the new content is.**
Under a correct linear spec with homoskedastic independent noise, Var(τ̂) = σ²ΔxᵀΣ⁻¹Δx/n is OLS leverage at the counterfactual point. Reviewers will say so. Also: with a noise-free outcome and a correct spec the error is exactly 0, so the whole P1 story is carried by the noise model (which the Brief lists only as "noise level swept") and by dependence among units (features share neighbours, so the iid sandwich formula need not give the right scaling or effective n). Make the test of P1 the *departure*: fit the exponent of n and d in log-log with CIs on graphs where the iid formula is expected to hold and where it is not (BA hubs, clustered designs), and report where the leverage formula over- or under-states the error. Also specify how D is computed with heterogeneous degree (pooled over units, degree-weighted, per-unit average of D²?): the per-unit formula d(1−p)/p and the pooled Mahalanobis distance differ on BA/Stanford3.

**3. P5 can be satisfied or failed for trivial reasons; the comparison class is missing.**
On a synthetic grid D is nearly a deterministic function of (d, p, n, design). A rank correlation of D with error "across settings" then mostly reproduces "degree and p predict error". Pre-specify benchmark predictors that D must beat: mean degree alone, p(1−p) alone, n·p(1−p)/d, and the estimator's own bootstrap SE. Also test *within* a setting across realisations/graph draws (does D computed from one experiment rank that experiment's error?), which is the claim "computable from one experiment" — across-cell correlation does not support it. shown.message:
Round 1 of the review is sent to `idea-repo` as issue #3, with the full text in the issue. I also recorded my commitment as `idea-review-repo`#2.

The review covers the Brief only. The Outline doesn't exist yet, so the plan review waits for it. I'll review again when the Brief changes or the Outline appears.

What it says:

- **Strengths:** a single falsifiable thesis, a frozen mechanism list, an exact estimand, and a willingness to report negative results.
- **Items 1, 3 and 5 (change what is measured):**
  - **Bias vs variance:** one quantity, D, can't explain both bias and variance. The bias from a curved response scales with raw exposure distance, which does not grow with degree. The variance follows the Mahalanobis distance, which does. P2 as written is therefore likely to fail for a reason known in advance, and the diagnostic needs two parts.
  - **P5 comparison class:** D is nearly a function of (d, p, n, design) on a synthetic grid. The Brief needs benchmark predictors that D must beat, a within-setting test, and an acceptance rule fixed before any runs.
  - **Metric:** RMSE relative to |τ| is unstable when τ is near 0.
- **Items 2, 4, 6 and 8:**
  - P1 is close to an OLS-leverage identity, so the new content has to be the departures from it.
  - Regression and exposure-mapping baselines need the same information.
  - The oracle baseline must be a legitimate error floor.
  - Cluster resolution decides P3, so it must be swept or fixed by a rule set in advance.
- **Remaining points:**
  - **Design:** the p grid can't test the symmetry claim; the flexible-learner arm needs a fixed tuning protocol; the variance sources need separating; the full cross of conditions won't fit in tens of CPU hours.
  - **Positioning:** two related papers are missing from `prior_work.md`. They are the data-adaptive exposure-threshold HT estimator (arXiv:2405.15887) and Shirani & Bayati (PNAS 2024) on causal message-passing. I read only their abstracts.

My searches were generic and turned up nothing that looked like the paper the objective bars.
